musrbeamsteer.gp_kg_minimizer.default_initial_coordinates(bounds: Sequence[Sequence[float]]) → list[ndarray]

Return a simple dimension-independent initial design.

It contains:

  • the centre of the parameter space;

  • one point at the lower boundary of each axis;

  • one point at the upper boundary of each axis;

while all other coordinates remain at their centre.

Number of points = 1 + 2*N.

Examples

N=1 -> 3 points N=2 -> 5 points N=4 -> 9 points

With initial_repeats=2 this uses 6, 10 and 18 measurements respectively.

Parameters:

bounds (sequence of sequence of float) – One finite (lower, upper) pair per dimension.

Returns:

The centre point plus one lower and upper axial point per dimension.

Return type:

list of numpy.ndarray

Raises:

ValueError – If bounds is invalid.

musrbeamsteer.gp_kg_minimizer.estimate_noise_variance(observations: Sequence[Observation]) → float

Estimate the common measurement-noise variance from repeated coordinates.

If two independent measurements at the same coordinate are

y1 = f(x) + e1 y2 = f(x) + e2

with Var(e)=sigma^2, then

E[(y1-y2)^2] = 2*sigma^2.

All same-coordinate pairs are pooled.

This assumes all measurements have the same statistical exposure.

Parameters:

observations (sequence of Observation) – Observations containing repeated coordinates and metrics.

Returns:

Estimated common observation-noise variance.

Return type:

float

Raises:

RuntimeError – If no coordinate has been measured more than once.

musrbeamsteer.gp_kg_minimizer.gp_kg_next_coordinate(observations: Sequence[Observation], bounds: Sequence[Sequence[float]], *, n_candidate_points: int = 192, n_decision_points: int = 1024, quadrature_order: int = 15, random_state: int = 0) → tuple[ndarray, float, float]

Choose the next coordinate using an approximate correlated Knowledge Gradient (KG).

Previously measured coordinates are included among the candidates, so the optimizer is allowed to repeat a point when replication is more useful than exploration.

Parameters:

  • observations – Existing observations, including at least one repeated coordinate.

  • bounds – Physical lower and upper bounds for each dimension.

  • n_candidate_points – Number of Sobol candidate points to evaluate.

  • n_decision_points – Number of Sobol points approximating the final decision space.

  • quadrature_order – Hermite quadrature order for the expected improvement estimate.

  • random_state – Seed controlling Sobol sampling and GP fitting.

Returns:

  • coordinate (ndarray) – Proposed next coordinate in physical parameter units.

  • kg (float) – Expected one-step value of the measurement, in metric units.

  • noise_std (float) – Current estimated standard deviation of one measurement.

Raises:

ValueError – If fewer than two observations are supplied.

musrbeamsteer.gp_kg_minimizer.search_minimum(accuracy: float, bounds: Sequence[Sequence[float]], get_measurement: Callable[[ndarray], Any], extract_metrics: Callable[[Sequence[Any]], Sequence[float]], *, initial_coordinates: Iterable[Sequence[float]] | None = None, initial_repeats: int = 2, max_measurements: int = 30, minimum_step_sizes: Sequence[float] | None = None, precisions: Sequence[int] | None = None, random_state: int = 12345, n_candidate_points: int = 192, n_decision_points: int = 1024, progress_callback: Callable[[Sequence[Observation], float | None], None] | None = None, verbose: bool = True) → SearchResult

Sequentially search for a noisy minimum.

Parameters:

  • accuracy – Stop when the current one-step Knowledge Gradient is below this value. Units are the CURRENT units returned by extract_metrics().

  • bounds – [(min_1,max_1), …, (min_N,max_N)].

  • get_measurement –

    User callback:

    measurement = get_measurement(coordinate)

  • extract_metrics –

    Global user callback:

    metrics = extract_metrics(all_measurements)

    It receives EVERY measurement collected so far and must return one scalar metric per measurement, in the same order. It is re-run after every new sequential measurement, so earlier metrics may change. This is suitable for PCA and other global analyses.

  • initial_coordinates – User-specified starting coordinates. They do NOT need to be extrema. If None, default_initial_coordinates(bounds) is used only as a convenience fallback.

  • minimum_step_sizes – Minimum per-dimension change between successive non-repeated measurements. A proposed change smaller than the configured value is expanded in the proposed direction, subject to the bounds. Repeated initial measurements are preserved for noise estimation.

  • precisions – Number of decimal places allowed for each coordinate. Proposed, measured, reported, and final coordinates are rounded accordingly.

  • initial_repeats – Number of measurements at each initial coordinate. Normally >=2 so the unknown absolute noise can be estimated.

  • progress_callback –

    Optional callback after all current metrics have been recomputed:

    progress_callback(observations, estimated_noise_std)

    Every Observation.metric is the CURRENT globally recomputed value.

Returns:

The estimated minimum and complete observation history.

Return type:

SearchResult

Raises:

  • ValueError – If search settings or callback results are invalid.

  • RuntimeError – If no measurements are acquired.
